releases.name: v0.7.1 — on npm
releases.body:
opencode-discuss is now on npm: <https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-discuss>. No code changes to the discussion itself; this release is about installing it.

## Install from npm

Add the package name to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{ "package": "opencode-discuss", "options": { "python": "python3" } }
```

Then install the two agent files and reload:

```sh
npx opencode-discuss              # add --dry-run to only see what it would do
```

Python 3.12 is still a separate requirement. Building from source works as before.

## What changed

- **Light install.** `@opencode/*`, `@opentui/*` and `solid-js` come from OpenCode itself, so they are now optional peer dependencies. Installing the package pulls **one** package (before this change: 424).
- **Small package.** 11 files, about 65 kB: the built plugin, the Python runner, the agent files, README and LICENSE. No tests or internal docs.
- **`npx opencode-discuss`** installs the agents (`--dry-run`, `--target DIR`, `--help`).
- The README images use absolute URLs, so they show on the npm page.
- `prepublishOnly` builds, typechecks and runs the unit and Python tests before every publish.

## Verified

- The published package installed from the registry into an empty folder: one package, the agent installer runs.
- An isolated OpenCode with `plugins: ["opencode-discuss"]` loaded it from the registry: server and TUI reached `ready`, no host failures.
- 222 unit tests and 43 Python bridge tests pass; CI is green.

**Full changes:** [v0.7.0...v0.7.1](https://github.com/thejohnd0e/opencode-discuss/compare/v0.7.0...v0.7.1)

releases.name: v0.7.0 — ledger-based conclusion, review by the other side
releases.body:
The joint conclusion is now built on the claim ledger, and the other side can check it. Installation and tests also work better on macOS and Linux.

## A conclusion that follows the ledger

A reviewer found that a claim from the very last reply had been listed as a disagreement, although nobody had a turn left to answer it. Open claims now have two distinct states:

- **skipped by the opponent**: the opponent had a turn after it and did not answer. This is a disagreement.
- **left open: the debate ended**: it came in the last reply. This is **not** a disagreement.

With a ledger, the conclusion gets the claims grouped by state and has four sections: *agreed*, *disagreed*, *left open when the debate ended*, *recommended next steps*. It is told to rely on the ledger instead of reconstructing the debate.

## Review of the conclusion by the other side

`/discuss-settings conclusion=b review=on`: after the conclusion, the side that did not write it gets one request to list distortions, such as a point in the wrong section, an agreement that never happened, its own position misstated, or a claim from the last reply shown as a disagreement. If it finds none, it answers "No objections." It does not reopen the debate. The panel shows the review as "Review of the conclusion · by A", and the handoff puts it right after the conclusion.

- The reviewer gets the same section rules as the writer, so it does not demand a different structure.
- The review is **advisory**. If it fails, the run still completes with its conclusion, and the panel and handoff say the review was not received.
- The conclusion and the review read the whole discussion, so reasoning models think longer there. Both get an output cap of at least **12000 tokens**, lowered to a model's advertised limit when known. The start dialog counts this in the ceiling.

## Easier to install, works beyond Windows

- `bun run install-agents` copies the two agent files into `~/.config/opencode/agents/`. It leaves identical files alone and backs up a changed one first. Add `--dry-run` to only see what it would do.
- Without `options.python`, the plugin runs `python` on Windows and `python3` on macOS and Linux.
- The smoke tests find `opencode` on `PATH` (or `OPENCODE_BIN`) and use the system temp directory.
- `.gitattributes` keeps LF line endings on every platform.
- The runner no longer has a default model pair, and local test-machine details were removed from the docs.

## Verified

- **Live runs** (DeepSeek Flash vs GPT-6 Luna, 3-round debates):
  - A claim from the last reply is now filed as "left open", not as a disagreement.
  - In one run the review caught a real distortion: a claim accepted only in part was listed as fully agreed. Two of its other objections asked for a different structure, which led to the section-rules fix.
  - After the fixes, a full run completed with 8 of 8 calls, the conclusion matching the ledger and "No objections." ($0.004).
- **Not yet seen live:** a failed review completing the run, which is covered by tests.
- **Tests:** 222 unit tests and 43 Python bridge tests pass; typecheck, build and both smoke tests are OK.

**Full changes:** [v0.6.1...v0.7.0](https://github.com/thejohnd0e/opencode-discuss/compare/v0.6.1...v0.7.0)

releases.name: v0.6.1 — stricter quote check
releases.body:
A fix release for the debate quote check. No new features.

## Your own words do not count as an answer, wherever they appear

In a debate, a reply must quote the opponent's points and answer them. 0.6.0 already ignored the opponent's own `>` quote lines. A reviewer pointed out that the same trick still worked when the opponent repeated your phrase **inside their own sentence**, or when a quote was "your old phrase plus a few new words".

The check now also compares every quote with the replier's own earlier replies:

- Only runs of **four or more words** count as borrowed, so two or three shared words never make a quote suspicious.
- A quote that is **mostly (60%+) your own earlier words** is not counted as an answer. The panel shows "⚠ Quotes its own words back, not the opponent's". This holds whether the opponent repeated those words in a quote line, a nested `>>` quote, or inside a sentence.
- A quote that borrows **a substantial part (30–60%)** of your words still counts, with a warning: "1 quote largely repeats its own earlier words". A doubtful quote is flagged rather than a real answer being rejected.
- Anything below that is a normal quote.

## Verified without paid calls

- **Saved debates.** The new check was replayed on all seven saved live debates, 22 checked replies. No honest quote was flagged. The only new verdict is the known case from the review: a reply that had quoted its own earlier sentences back, now 0 counted, 2 recycled.
- **Tests.** Five regression tests cover a nested quote, your phrase inside the opponent's sentence, an old phrase with new words, a half-and-half quote, and an honest quote that shares a few words. 208 unit tests and 37 Python bridge tests pass.

**Full changes:** [v0.6.0...v0.6.1](https://github.com/thejohnd0e/opencode-discuss/compare/v0.6.0...v0.6.1)

releases.name: v0.6.0 — claim ledger
releases.body:
## Claim ledger

A debate now keeps track of every argument and what became of it.

Each debate reply ends with a short service block: its new claims, and a verdict on every open claim of the opponent (`rebutted` or `accepted`). The plugin does the bookkeeping:

- **Numbering.** It numbers the claims (A1, A2, B1…) itself.
- **Open claims.** It tells each side which of the opponent's claims are still open, so nothing gets lost three turns later.
- **Clean text.** The block is cut from the reply, even while it streams.

What you see:

- **Under each reply:** `• Answers A1 rebutted · new B1`. A warning appears when a claim of the opponent was left open, or when the block could not be read.
- **Below the discussion:** a **Claims** list with each claim and its state: never answered, rebutted or accepted by the opponent.
- **Conclusion:** written from the ledger. Accepted claims are candidates for *agreed*; rebutted and unanswered ones go to *disagreed*, and unanswered ones are named as such.
- **Handoff:** a **Claims ledger** section listing every claim with its author's model and its fate.

Accepting a good argument is a valid way to close a claim, not a failure: only claims left without an answer are flagged.

## Fixes found in live debates

- **A block without its opening tag is read.** One model wrote the ledger lines and `[/ledger]` but never `[ledger]`, and all of its claims and verdicts were lost. A block is now also found by its closing tag, or as a trailing run of claim and verdict lines. Markdown emphasis, bullets, dashes and a code fence around the block are tolerated too.
- **Two quotes on adjacent lines are two quotes.** They used to be joined into one passage and reported as "not found".
- **Recycled quotes no longer count.** Only the opponent's own words count as an answer. A reviewer noticed that a model could quote back its own earlier sentence, taken from the opponent's `>` lines, and pass the check. Such quotes are now flagged: "quotes its own words back, not the opponent's".
- **The first failed reply ends the run.** A provider error, timeout, empty reply, or an output limit used up by reasoning now stops the run, with no further replies and no conclusion. Before, the run went on: in a debate the other side answered the same old reply again and again, and the run cost more.
- **A warning for small caps in a debate.** A debate reply carries quotes, answers and a claims block. Below 3000 tokens per reply, reasoning models can use up the cap before writing anything, so the start dialog and `/discuss-settings` now warn.

## Verified

A live 3-round debate on OpenCode 2.2.5 (DeepSeek Flash vs GPT-6 Luna, 6000 tokens, conclusion by B): completed with 7 of 7 requests, $0.0047.

- Every reply's ledger was read, and every open claim was answered on the next turn: two rebutted, five accepted.
- Only the last claim stayed open, as it must.
- Replaying that run with the recycled-quote fix flags exactly the one reply that quoted its own words back.

207 unit tests, 32 Python bridge tests and both smoke tests pass.

**Full changes:** [v0.5.0...v0.6.0](https://github.com/thejohnd0e/opencode-discuss/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0)

releases.name: v0.5.0 — debate that answers the opponent
releases.body:
## Debate that answers the opponent

In `debate` mode the two models now have to engage with each other's arguments instead of taking turns at their own monologues.

```
/discuss-settings mode=debate rounds=2
```

- From the second reply on, every reply starts with one or two **verbatim quotes** from the opponent's last reply (lines starting with `>`). Each quote is followed by an answer to it: rebutted with a reason, or accepted. Only then comes at most one new argument.
- The runner **checks the quotes** against what the opponent actually said. Quote marks, case, punctuation, an ellipsis or a slipped word do not matter. A paraphrase, reordered words or an invented quote do not count.
- The panel shows the result under each reply: `✓ Answers 2 points of the opponent`, or a warning when a reply quoted nothing or quoted something the opponent never said. The handoff flags such replies too.
- No extra request is made for this. `cooperative` and `critical` are unchanged.

## Replies in the topic's language, for real this time

In 0.4.0 the rule "answer in the language of the topic" was written in Russian, like the built-in prompts, and one model still answered an English topic in Russian. The rule now quotes the topic, and for a topic in Latin script it is written in English ("not in Russian"). It also follows a topic change during the run.

## Verified

A live debate on OpenCode 2.2.5 (DeepSeek Flash vs GPT-6 Luna, 2 rounds, conclusion by B): completed with 5 of 5 requests, $0.0013.

- All three checked replies quoted the opponent twice, and every quote was real.
- One side explicitly changed its position on two points it could not defend.
- The conclusion separated what was agreed in the debate from what was still disputed.
- Every reply and the conclusion were in English.

193 unit tests, 21 Python bridge tests and both smoke tests pass.

## Next

A claim ledger (A1, B2… with open / rebutted / accepted states) and a conclusion built from it.

**Full changes:** [v0.4.0...v0.5.0](https://github.com/thejohnd0e/opencode-discuss/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0)
